children: Shares of Sammaan Capital Ltd. will be in focus on Monday, November 16, after the company reported a strong sequential recovery in its September quarter (Q2FY27) performance, with profit after tax (PAT) rising 28% quarter-on-quarter to ₹312 crore from ₹243 crore in the previous quarter.

The company's disbursements increased 62% sequentially to ₹6,278 crore, compared to ₹3,875 crore in the June quarter. Assets under management (AUM) grew 5.2% quarter-on-quarter to ₹59,188 crore from ₹56,239 crore.
Asset quality also improved, with the gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio declining to 0.15% from 0.21% in the previous quarter, a reduction of 6 basis points.
Interest income rose 7.7% sequentially to ₹1,161 crore from ₹1,078 crore. Finance costs, meanwhile, declined 2.7% to ₹1,299 crore from ₹1,335 crore.
Net interest income (NII) stood at negative ₹138 crore, compared with negative ₹257 crore in the previous quarter. The company also reported fair-value gains of ₹648 crore.
What management said during the earnings call
During the earnings call, the management said lending rates had been increased by 25 basis points from November. The company's cost of funds stood at 9.8%, compared with 10% in the previous quarter.

Sammaan Capital also secured over $150 million in funding from a UAE-based bank. The company retained its FY27 PAT guidance at ₹1,400 crore and said it was targeting an improvement in gross lending margins to 3.5%, from the current level of around 2.9%.
Sammaan Capital shares settled 0.21% higher at ₹137.80 on Friday. However, the stock has declined around 5% so far this year.

title: Sammaan Capital shares in focus after Q2 results, profit guidance retained for the year
